```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(toxval)
ambient_omega <- 3.5
published_omega <- 2.81
paper_year <- 2025L
paper_table <- 1L
paper_volume <- 8L
paper_article <- 1518L
licence_version <- "3.0"
download_date <- as.Date("2026-10-23")
adjacent_ambient_stations <- 9L
bootstrap_n <- 4000L
sig_level <- 0.005
omega_levels <- c(3.5, 3.0, 2.5)
paper_cover <- c(5.24, 3.66, 2.54)
paper_se <- c(1.00, 0.66, 0.70)
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(fmt(100 * x, digits), "%")
toxval_source <- Sys.getenv("TOXVAL_SOURCE", unset = getwd())
toxval_commit <- tryCatch(
  system2("git", c("-C", shQuote(toxval_source), "rev-parse", "HEAD"),
    stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE
  ),
  error = function(e) "not recorded",
  warning = function(w) "not recorded"
)
```

## Study and data

Noonan, Birrell, Fisher and Fabricius (`r paper_year`) studied reef communities
along a natural carbon dioxide gradient at the Upa-Upasina seeps. For each
station, quadrat photographs provided benthic percent cover (e.g. of
*Acropora*). Seawater measurements were used to calculate station mean
aragonite saturation state (ΩAr); for `r adjacent_ambient_stations` ambient
stations without their own measurements, the authors assigned the average
chemistry of adjacent ambient stations. Their data are
available in the [AIMS data record](https://apps.aims.gov.au/metadata/view/76c40b3c-8535-43b6-bf5f-ad26d6e1ad92),
and the analysis is reported in [*Communications Biology*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-025-08889-w).
The no-significant-effect concentration (NSEC) asks how far ΩAr can fall from
the ambient value of `r fmt(ambient_omega, 1)` before fitted *Acropora* cover
first differs significantly from cover at ambient ΩAr. The
[NSEC definition](https://open-aims.github.io/toxval/articles/nsec-definition.html)
describes this comparison for other fitted curves.

```{r}
#| label: data
#| include: false
seep <- oa_seep_cover
stopifnot(
  nrow(seep) == 37L,
  all(is.finite(seep$OmAr.mean)),
  all(seep$ACROPORA >= 0 & seep$ACROPORA <= 100)
)
```

The packaged `oa_seep_cover` data contain `r nrow(seep)` station means, with
ΩAr from `r fmt(min(seep$OmAr.mean))` to
`r fmt(max(seep$OmAr.mean))`. The `ACROPORA` column gives percent cover of
*Acropora* at each station, while `OmAr.mean` gives the corresponding station
mean ΩAr.

## The predictor and ambient control

We expressed exposure as the reduction from ambient ΩAr, so that increasing
`om_deficit` means stronger acidification as ΩAr falls. A deficit of zero
therefore denotes the ambient control. `x_control = 0` makes
`toxval_predict()` start its prediction grid at that control. `nsec()` searches
upward for the first decrease beyond a reference response (a lower quantile of
predicted cover at ambient).

```{r}
#| label: predictor
seep$om_deficit <- ambient_omega - seep$OmAr.mean
range(seep$om_deficit)
```

```{r}
#| label: predictor-checks
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  min(seep$om_deficit) < 0,
  max(seep$om_deficit) > 0,
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    ambient_omega - max(seep$om_deficit), min(seep$OmAr.mean)
  ))
)
```

Some observed stations have ΩAr above ambient, so their deficits are negative
(down to `r fmt(min(seep$om_deficit))`). The grid used for the NSEC begins at
zero and ends at the largest observed deficit of
`r fmt(max(seep$om_deficit))`.

## Quasibinomial fit

The paper fitted percent cover against ΩAr with a quasibinomial generalised
linear model. We used the same family and logit link for station mean
*Acropora* cover, with the reduction from ambient as predictor. This changes
the sign of the slope, while the fitted responses are identical.

```{r}
#| label: fit
fit <- stats::glm(
  ACROPORA / 100 ~ om_deficit,
  data = seep,
  family = quasibinomial
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-comparison
#| include: false
fit_omega <- stats::glm(
  ACROPORA / 100 ~ OmAr.mean, data = seep, family = quasibinomial
)
paper_predictions <- stats::predict(
  fit,
  newdata = data.frame(om_deficit = ambient_omega - omega_levels),
  type = "response", se.fit = TRUE
)
fitted_cover <- 100 * paper_predictions$fit
fitted_se <- 100 * paper_predictions$se.fit
table_gap <- max(abs(c(fitted_cover - paper_cover, fitted_se - paper_se)))
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(stats::fitted(fit)), unname(stats::fitted(fit_omega)))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    unname(stats::coef(fit)[["om_deficit"]]),
    -unname(stats::coef(fit_omega)[["OmAr.mean"]])
  )),
  table_gap < 0.01
)
```

At ΩAr `r fmt(omega_levels[1], 1)`, fitted cover (standard error) is
`r fmt(fitted_cover[1])` (`r fmt(fitted_se[1])`)% against
`r fmt(paper_cover[1])` (`r fmt(paper_se[1])`)% in Table `r paper_table` of
Noonan et al. (`r paper_year`). At ΩAr `r fmt(omega_levels[2], 1)`, the
corresponding values are `r fmt(fitted_cover[2])` (`r fmt(fitted_se[2])`)% and
`r fmt(paper_cover[2])` (`r fmt(paper_se[2])`)%; at ΩAr
`r fmt(omega_levels[3], 1)`, they are `r fmt(fitted_cover[3])`
(`r fmt(fitted_se[3])`)% and `r fmt(paper_cover[3])`
(`r fmt(paper_se[3])`)%. The largest difference from the published means or
standard errors is `r fmt(table_gap, 3)` percentage points.

For a quasibinomial fit, dispersion is estimated from the data, which allows
the variability among stations to differ from the binomial variance.
`toxval_predict()` draws coefficient vectors jointly from a multivariate
normal distribution with mean `coef(fit)` and covariance `vcov(fit)`. Each
vector defines a full predicted curve, called a realisation. We converted the
proportions to percent cover and used the
`r fmt(100 * (0.975 - 0.025), 0)`% pointwise quantiles of
`r bootstrap_n` realisations for the blue band.

```{r}
#| label: predictions
#| include: false
pred <- toxval_predict(
  fit, x_var = "om_deficit", x_control = 0, n_boot = bootstrap_n, seed = 42
)
band <- apply(pred$curves[[1]], 2, stats::quantile,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975)
)
curve <- data.frame(
  om_deficit = pred$x_vec,
  fitted = 100 * stats::predict(
    fit, newdata = data.frame(om_deficit = pred$x_vec), type = "response"
  ),
  lower = 100 * band[1, ],
  upper = 100 * band[2, ]
)
slope <- coef(summary(fit))["om_deficit", "Estimate"]
slope_se <- coef(summary(fit))["om_deficit", "Std. Error"]
fitted_stations <- 100 * stats::fitted(fit)
largest_residual <- which.max(abs(seep$ACROPORA - fitted_stations))
n_zero_cover <- sum(seep$ACROPORA == 0)
stopifnot(
  identical(pred$x_vec[1], 0),
  nrow(pred$curves[[1]]) == bootstrap_n,
  isTRUE(all.equal(max(pred$x_vec), max(seep$om_deficit))),
  slope < 0,
  all(diff(curve$fitted) < 0),
  curve$fitted[1] > tail(curve$fitted, 1),
  n_zero_cover > 0,
  abs(seep$ACROPORA[largest_residual] - fitted_stations[largest_residual]) > 5,
  all(curve$lower < curve$fitted & curve$fitted < curve$upper)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-glm-curve
#| fig-cap: "Station mean *Acropora* cover against the reduction in ΩAr from ambient (points), with the fitted quasibinomial curve (black) and a pointwise interval from the toxval realisations (blue). The vertical dotted line marks ambient ΩAr."
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot2::ggplot(curve, ggplot2::aes(om_deficit)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = fitted)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = ACROPORA), data = seep) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Reduction from ambient ΩAr",
    y = "Acropora cover (%)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

Across the stations, observed *Acropora* cover ranges from
`r fmt(min(seep$ACROPORA))` to `r fmt(max(seep$ACROPORA))`%, with zero cover at
`r n_zero_cover` of `r nrow(seep)` stations (@fig-glm-curve).
The fitted cover declines from `r fmt(curve$fitted[1])`% at ambient ΩAr to
`r fmt(tail(curve$fitted, 1))`% at the largest observed deficit. At ambient,
the pointwise interval from the realisations runs from
`r fmt(curve$lower[1])` to `r fmt(curve$upper[1])`%; at the largest deficit,
it runs from `r fmt(tail(curve$lower, 1))` to
`r fmt(tail(curve$upper, 1))`%. However, individual station cover differs from
the mean curve: for example, at ΩAr
`r fmt(seep$OmAr.mean[largest_residual])`, observed cover is
`r fmt(seep$ACROPORA[largest_residual])`% (fitted cover
`r fmt(fitted_stations[largest_residual])`%). This difference may reflect
variation among stations beyond mean ΩAr.

## The no-significant-effect concentration

Noonan et al. (`r paper_year`) defined the NSEC as the ΩAr where the predicted
response first differs from that at ambient beyond its
`r fmt(100 * (1 - 2 * sig_level), 0)`% confidence interval. The paper does not
specify the scale or critical distribution used for that interval. We
reconstructed its point estimate from the lower normal limit on the logit scale
at ambient, then found where the fitted curve crosses that response.

```{r}
#| label: published-reference
ambient_link <- stats::predict(
  fit, newdata = data.frame(om_deficit = 0), type = "link", se.fit = TRUE
)
normal_limit <- stats::qnorm(1 - sig_level)
lower_link <- ambient_link$fit - normal_limit * ambient_link$se.fit
paper_reference <- fit$family$linkinv(lower_link)
paper_deficit <- (lower_link - ambient_link$fit) / slope
paper_omega <- unname(ambient_omega - paper_deficit)
paper_omega
```

```{r}
#| label: reference-checks
#| include: false
control_proportion <- fit$family$linkinv(ambient_link$fit)
response_se <- control_proportion * (1 - control_proportion) * ambient_link$se.fit
response_reference <- control_proportion - normal_limit * response_se
t_link <- ambient_link$fit -
  stats::qt(1 - sig_level, stats::df.residual(fit)) * ambient_link$se.fit
response_omega <- ambient_omega -
  (stats::qlogis(response_reference) - ambient_link$fit) / slope
t_omega <- ambient_omega - (t_link - ambient_link$fit) / slope
stopifnot(
  round(paper_omega, 2) == published_omega,
  abs(response_omega - paper_omega) > 0.2,
  abs(t_omega - paper_omega) > 0.03,
  paper_reference > 0,
  paper_reference < control_proportion
)
```

The reconstructed lower ambient response is `r pct(paper_reference, 3)` cover.
The fitted curve crosses it at ΩAr `r fmt(paper_omega, 3)`, which rounds to the
`r fmt(published_omega)` in Table `r paper_table` of the paper. A normal limit
on the response scale would give ΩAr `r fmt(response_omega, 3)`; a *t* limit
on the logit scale would give `r fmt(t_omega, 3)`. A two-sided
`r fmt(100 * (1 - 2 * sig_level), 0)`% interval has a lower tail of
`r pct(sig_level, 1)`, so we used `sig_val = 0.005` to set the corresponding
quantile of predicted ambient cover in toxval.

```{r}
#| label: nsec-glm
ns <- nsec(
  fit, x_var = "om_deficit", x_control = 0,
  sig_val = 0.005, n_boot = 4000, seed = 42
)
ns_dec <- ns[ns$direction == "decreasing", ]
ns_dec[, c("direction", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "control", "reference")]
```

```{r}
#| label: nsec-checks
#| include: false
omega_estimate <- ambient_omega - ns_dec$estimate
omega_low_bound <- ambient_omega - ns_dec$conf.high
omega_high <- ambient_omega - ns_dec$conf.low
stopifnot(
  nrow(ns_dec) == 1L,
  ns_dec$sig_val == sig_level,
  ns_dec$reference < ns_dec$control,
  ns_dec$estimate > 0,
  ns_dec$conf.low < ns_dec$estimate,
  ns_dec$estimate < ns_dec$conf.high,
  omega_low_bound < omega_estimate,
  omega_estimate < omega_high
)
```

For the specified seed, `nsec()` takes the lower
`r pct(sig_level, 1)` quantile of ambient cover across the realisations as its
reference. The decreasing row gives a median crossing
`r fmt(ns_dec$estimate, 3)` ΩAr units below ambient, with a lower interval
limit of `r fmt(ns_dec$conf.low, 3)` and an upper limit of at least
`r fmt(ns_dec$conf.high, 3)` units. The median control response is
`r pct(ns_dec$control, 2)` cover and the reference is
`r pct(ns_dec$reference, 2)` cover. Expressed as ΩAr, the median NSEC is
`r fmt(omega_estimate, 3)`, with an interval from at most
`r fmt(omega_low_bound, 3)` to `r fmt(omega_high, 3)`. The bound on the lower
ΩAr limit follows from the censored realisations described below.

## Interval and censoring

```{r}
#| label: censor-checks
#| include: false
warning_text <- character()
ns_draws <- withCallingHandlers(
  nsec(
    fit, x_var = "om_deficit", x_control = 0,
    sig_val = 0.005, n_boot = 4000, seed = 42, draws = TRUE
  ),
  warning = function(w) {
    warning_text <<- c(warning_text, conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
dec_draws <- ns_draws$draws[[which(ns_draws$direction == "decreasing")]]$value.draw
inc_draws <- ns_draws$draws[[which(ns_draws$direction == "increasing")]]$value.draw
n_dec_censored <- sum(is.infinite(dec_draws))
n_inc_censored <- sum(is.infinite(inc_draws))
# each realisation is linear on the logit scale, so its slope is read from its
# first two grid values; `pred` and `ns_draws` share seed 42
logit_curves <- stats::qlogis(pred$curves[[1]])
slope_draws <- (logit_curves[, 2] - logit_curves[, 1]) / diff(pred$x_vec[1:2])
n_nonnegative <- sum(slope_draws >= 0)
n_shallow <- sum(is.infinite(dec_draws) & slope_draws < 0)
stopifnot(
  length(warning_text) == 1L,
  grepl("Some realisations have no crossing", warning_text),
  identical(ns_draws$estimate, ns$estimate),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    unname(ns_draws$control[ns_draws$direction == "decreasing"]),
    unname(ns_dec$control)
  )),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    ns_dec$estimate,
    unname(stats::quantile(dec_draws, 0.5, type = 1))
  )),
  slope_se / abs(slope) > 0.4,
  ns_dec$conf.high - ns_dec$conf.low > ns_dec$estimate,
  isTRUE(all.equal(ns_dec$conf.high, max(seep$om_deficit))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(omega_low_bound, min(seep$OmAr.mean))),
  n_dec_censored / length(dec_draws) > 0.025,
  n_nonnegative > 0,
  all(is.infinite(dec_draws[slope_draws >= 0])),
  n_shallow > 0,
  n_dec_censored == n_nonnegative + n_shallow,
  n_inc_censored / length(inc_draws) > 0.99,
  !anyNA(dec_draws),
  !anyNA(inc_draws)
)
```

The deficit slope is `r fmt(slope, 3)` on the logit scale, with a standard
error of `r fmt(slope_se, 3)` (`r pct(slope_se / abs(slope), 0)` of its
magnitude). For a declining realisation whose control is above the reference,
the crossing deficit is approximately the difference between their logits
divided by the magnitude of that realisation's slope. Shallow negative slopes
therefore put crossings far from ambient. Of the `r bootstrap_n` realisations,
`r n_nonnegative` (`r pct(n_nonnegative / bootstrap_n)`) have a slope at or
above zero and never cross the decreasing reference; another `r n_shallow`
with a negative slope do not cross within the grid.

In the decreasing direction, `r n_dec_censored` of `r length(dec_draws)`
realisations are censored (`r pct(n_dec_censored / length(dec_draws))`), above
the `r pct(0.025)` upper tail. The upper deficit quantile is therefore
censored, and `nsec()` prints a warning. The interval spans at least
`r fmt(ns_dec$conf.high - ns_dec$conf.low, 3)` deficit units: its reported
upper limit is a lower bound at the last grid value. The corresponding lower
ΩAr limit is an upper bound, so the interval does not locate that limit within
the observed ΩAr range. Extending `x_range` could locate further crossings,
but would require prediction below the observed ΩAr range.

In the increasing direction, `r n_inc_censored` of `r length(inc_draws)`
realisations have no crossing, as the fitted response declines. No
realisation lacked a reference, although the warning includes that possibility.

## Comparison with the published method

```{r}
#| label: comparison-checks
#| include: false
fitted_cross_omega <- ambient_omega -
  (stats::qlogis(ns_dec$reference) - ambient_link$fit) / slope
reference_gap <- 100 * abs(ns_dec$reference - paper_reference)
seed_values <- c(42L, seq_len(12L))
omega_by_seed <- vapply(seed_values, function(this_seed) {
  if (this_seed == pred$meta$seed) return(omega_estimate)
  this_ns <- suppressWarnings(nsec(
    fit, x_var = "om_deficit", x_control = 0,
    sig_val = sig_level, n_boot = bootstrap_n, seed = this_seed
  ))
  ambient_omega - this_ns$estimate[this_ns$direction == "decreasing"]
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(
  length(omega_by_seed) == length(seed_values),
  reference_gap < 0.1,
  abs(fitted_cross_omega - omega_estimate) < 0.02,
  min(omega_by_seed) < paper_omega,
  paper_omega < max(omega_by_seed),
  sum(round(omega_by_seed, 2) == published_omega) == 2L
)
```

Both calculations use the quasibinomial fit and one lower reference for
ambient cover. The toxval reference differs from the reconstructed paper
reference by `r fmt(reference_gap, 3)` percentage points. The fitted curve
crosses the toxval reference at ΩAr `r fmt(fitted_cross_omega, 3)`, close to
the median crossing for the specified seed. This proximity may explain the
numerical agreement in this run. Across `r length(seed_values)`
runs (seed `r seed_values[1]` and seeds `r min(seed_values[-1])` to
`r max(seed_values[-1])`), the median ΩAr NSEC ranges from
`r fmt(min(omega_by_seed), 3)` to `r fmt(max(omega_by_seed), 3)`.
Although the reconstructed point estimate is within that range, only
`r sum(round(omega_by_seed, 2) == published_omega)` of those estimates round
to the paper's `r fmt(published_omega)`.

Whereas the paper's Table `r paper_table` gives point NSECs without intervals,
toxval adds a `r fmt(100 * (0.975 - 0.025), 0)`% interval from the crossings
of the realisations. Inverting a pointwise band on the response would not generally
give an interval with the stated coverage for the predictor at a crossing,
particularly where the fitted curve is nearly flat. The
[drc case study](https://open-aims.github.io/toxval/articles/case-drc.html)
examines that interval distinction for an effect concentration.

```{r}
#| label: provenance
#| comment: ""
cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", "toxval", as.character(utils::packageVersion("toxval"))))
cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", "commit", toxval_commit))
for (pkg in c("ggplot2", "knitr")) {
  cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", pkg, as.character(utils::packageVersion(pkg))))
}
cat(sprintf("%-10s %s\n", "R", getRversion()))
```

- Source: Noonan, Birrell, Fisher and Fabricius (`r paper_year`),
  ["Progressive changes in coral reef communities with increasing ocean acidification"](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-025-08889-w),
  *Communications Biology* `r paper_volume`, `r paper_article`.
- Data: `oa_seep_cover`, derived from that paper and held in
  the [AIMS data record](https://apps.aims.gov.au/metadata/view/76c40b3c-8535-43b6-bf5f-ad26d6e1ad92)
  and downloaded on `r format(download_date, "%Y-%m-%d")` under Creative
  Commons Attribution `r licence_version` Australia.
- Fit: `stats::glm()` with a quasibinomial family and a logit link, with
  station mean cover as the response.
- Realisations: `r length(dec_draws)` parametric bootstrap curves with seed
  `r pred$meta$seed`; the default grid has `r length(pred$x_vec)` values from ambient
  to the largest observed deficit.
- The commit line identifies the toxval checkout used for the render.
